contributions.headingText: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour (MPNST) is a malignant neoplasm usually showing spindle cell morphology, which arises from a peripheral nerve, from a pre-existing benign nerve sheath tumour, or in a patient with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). Outside of these settings, the diagnosis of sporadic or radiation-associated MPNST is challenging and requires histological and immunohistochemical evidence suggesting Schwannian differentiation.

2B5E & XH2XP8 Malignant nerve sheath tumour of peripheral nerves or autonomic nervous system, primary site & Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour

2B5E & XH4V81 Malignant nerve sheath tumour of peripheral nerves or autonomic nervous system, primary site & Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour, epithelioid

2B5E & XH2VV8 Malignant nerve sheath tumour of peripheral nerves or autonomic nervous system, primary site & Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour with rhabdomyoblastic differentiation
Not recommended: malignant schwannoma; neurofibrosarcoma; neurogenic sarcoma.

MPNSTs occur in the lung, chest wall, and all mediastinal compartments, most commonly in the paraspinal area; along the vagus nerve; or centred on the pleura, hilum, or bronchovascular bundle {25595633; 24133387; 24282191}.
Presenting symptoms include pain, dyspnoea, cough, and weight loss {25595633; 18292741}. Imaging shows a large, invasive, PET-avid mass {24133387; 18292741}.

The chest is an uncommon site for MPNSTs {6665754}, which tend to occur in older adults (seventh decade of life) but have a wide age range {25595633}. About 50% of cases occur in patients with NF1, 10% are radiation-related, and the rest are sporadic {3082508}.
MPNST may be associated with irradiation or NF1 {3082508}.

Complex structural and numerical chromosomal abnormalities and biallelic mutations in NF1 are common in MPNST {10398430; 19142971}. Frequent coexisting loss-of-function mutations occur in the genes of three pathways: NF1, CDKN2A/CDKN2B, and PRC2 core components (EED or SUZ12) {25240281; 25119042; 25305755; 30722027}. In NF1, histological progression from neurofibroma to MPNST is accompanied by progressive genomic alterations in these pathways, as well as increased copy-number variations {21987445; 25240281; 30722027}. About 80% of conventional MPNSTs exhibit loss of PRC2 activity due to mutations in EED or SUZ12, as well as loss of H3K27me3 expression {26645727; 25240281; 26585554}.

Epithelioid MPNSTs are genetically distinct. SMARCB1 inactivation with SMARCB1 (INI1) loss by immunohistochemistry is observed in approximately 75% of cases {30864974}, whereas these tumours rarely have alterations in the three pathways listed above {25240281; 28368924}.
MPNSTs are large (up to 270 mm) circumscribed white-yellow masses {3082508; 25595633; 18292741; 24282191}. They may be oblong, extending along a nerve {3082508; 24133387}.

Thoracic MPNSTs are usually composed of densely cellular monomorphic spindled cells growing in fascicles, with alternating cellularity, perivascular cellular condensation, and herniation into vascular lumina {3082508}. NF1-associated MPNSTs may arise from diffuse or plexiform neurofibromas {3082508} and may contain structures resembling Wagner–Meissner bodies {25595633}. Thoracic MPNSTs are usually high-grade, with numerous mitoses and necrosis. MPNSTs may show divergent differentiation, including rhabdomyoblasts, glands, bone, or cartilage {3082508}. Rare epithelioid MPNSTs consist of nests and sheets of relatively uniform epithelioid cells with prominent nucleoli.

Conventional spindled MPNSTs show patchy weak expression of S100 and SOX10, or they may be entirely negative. Loss of H3K27me3 expression is supportive in the appropriate morphological context, but it is not specific for MPNST {26585554}. Epithelioid MPNSTs show diffuse S100 and SOX10 expression, retained H3K27me3, and loss of SMARCB1 (INI1) in a significant subset.

Conventional MPNST

Essential:

  • Monomorphic fascicular spindle cell sarcoma with limited pleomorphism
  • Sarcoma arising from nerve, pre-existing benign nerve sheath tumour, or in patient with NF1
  • Sporadic soft tissue spindle cell sarcoma with evidence of Schwannian lineage (focal S100/SOX10)
Epithelioid MPNST

Essential:

  • Sporadic malignant epithelioid neoplasm with diffuse S100/SOX10 expression and loss of SMARCB1

Thoracic malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumours are aggressive sarcomas with a mortality rate of 60% {25595633; 18292741}. Truncal location, tumour size > 50 mm, local recurrence, high-grade morphology, association with NF1, and rhabdomyoblastic differentiation are adverse prognostic factors {27158754}.
